tools.name: read
tools.description: Use when you need to read one public web page: fetches the URL live and returns its main readable content as clean Markdown (or plain text), with navigation, ads, cookie banners and boilerplate removed, plus title, byline, publish date, language and word count. Respects robots.txt. Server-rendered H

tools.name: meta
tools.description: Use when you need a link preview or page metadata: fetches the URL live and returns title, description, site name, canonical URL, language, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, preview image, favicon, author and publish date, RSS/Atom feeds, robots meta and JSON-LD (schema.org) types, after following r

tools.name: feed
tools.description: Use when you need the latest posts or headlines from a site, blog, newsroom, podcast or subreddit: give a feed URL or just the site URL (the RSS/Atom feed is auto-discovered from the page) and get normalized items with title, link, publish date (ISO 8601), author, summary, image and categories, newe

tools.name: links
tools.description: Use when you need the outgoing links of one page (crawling, SEO audits, finding a contact/pricing/docs page, link building): fetches the URL live (respects robots.txt) and returns every http(s) link resolved to an absolute URL, deduplicated, with anchor text (or image alt), internal vs external, rel

tools.name: sitemap
tools.description: Use when you need the list of pages a site publishes (to crawl it, find recent posts, or audit SEO): give a site URL (the sitemap is discovered from robots.txt Sitemap: lines, then /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /wp-sitemap.xml) or a sitemap URL directly. Returns the page URLs with lastmod, chang

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "read" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Use when you need to read one public web page: fetches the URL live and returns its main readable content as clean Markdown (or plain text), with navigation, ad…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read, meta, feed, links, sitemap · Private data: links · Public sink: read, meta, feed.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read, meta, feed, links, sitemap · Private data: links · Public sink: read, meta, feed

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
